sanskrit: duryodhanasya śūrasya śaraughāñ śīghram asyataḥ saṃkruddhasyāntakasyeva ko vegaṃ saṃsahed raṇe
english: When valiant Duryodhana hurls his floods of arrows swiftly, like Death himself enraged, who in battle could withstand his onslaught?

sanskrit: karṇena ca kṛto rājā vimukhaḥ śatrutāpanaḥ balavāṃl laghuhastaś ca kṛtī yuddhaviśāradaḥ
english: And by Karṇa, that scorcher of foes—strong, swift of hand, accomplished, and skilled in war—the king has been turned back.

sanskrit: rādheyaḥ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭhaṃ śaktaḥ pīḍayituṃ raṇe sahito dhṛtarāṣṭrasya putraiḥ śūro mahātmabhiḥ
english: Rādheya, that hero, joined with the high-souled sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, is able in battle to press hard even the foremost of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tasyaivaṃ yudhyamānasya saṃgrāme saṃyatātmanaḥ anyair api ca pārthasya hṛtaṃ varma mahārathaiḥ
english: As Pārtha fought thus in the engagement with self-possessed soul, his armor was stripped away even by other great chariot-warriors.

sanskrit: upavāsakṛśo rājā bhṛśaṃ bharatasattama brāhme bale sthito hy eṣa na kṣatre 'tibale vibho
english: Wasted by fasting, O best of the Bharatas, the king stands firm in the strength of the brahman, not, O lord, in the overwhelming strength of the warrior.

sanskrit: na jīvati mahārājo manye pārtha yudhiṣṭhiraḥ yad bhīmasenaḥ sahate siṃhanādam amarṣaṇaḥ
english: I think, O Pārtha, that the great king Yudhiṣṭhira no longer lives, since the wrathful Bhīmasena now endures these lion-roars.

sanskrit: nardatāṃ dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ punaḥ punar ariṃdama dhamatāṃ ca mahāśaṅkhān saṃgrāme jitakāśinām
english: of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O subduer of foes, who again and again roar and blow their great conches in the battle, flushed with the look of conquest—

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiraṃ pāṇḍaveyaṃ hateti bharatarṣabha saṃcodayaty asau karṇo dhārtarāṣṭrān mahābalān
english: "Yudhiṣṭhira the Pāṇḍava is slain!"—so, O bull of the Bharatas, does Karṇa urge on the mighty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra.

sanskrit: sthūṇākarṇendrajālena pārtha pāśupatena ca pracchādayanto rājānam anuyānti mahārathāḥ āturo me mato rājā saṃniṣevyaś ca bhārata
english: Veiling the king with the Sthūṇākarṇa, the Indrajāla, and the Pāśupata weapons, O Pārtha, the great chariot-warriors pursue him. I deem the king to be in distress, O Bhārata, and in need of being attended to.

sanskrit: yathainam anuvartante pāñcālāḥ saha pāṇḍavaiḥ tvaramāṇās tvarākāle sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varāḥ majjantam iva pātāle balino 'py ujjihīrṣavaḥ
english: For the Pāñcālas with the Pāṇḍavas, foremost of all weapon-bearers, follow after him in haste at this urgent hour, eager to lift him up though he sinks as it were into the abyss, mighty though he is.

sanskrit: na ketur dṛśyate rājñaḥ karṇena nihataḥ śaraiḥ paśyator yamayoḥ pārtha sātyakeś ca śikhaṇḍinaḥ
english: The king's banner is no longer seen, cut down by Karṇa's arrows, O Pārtha, before the very eyes of the twins, of Sātyaki, and of Śikhaṇḍin—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnasya bhīmasya śatānīkasya vā vibho pāñcālānāṃ ca sarveṣāṃ cedīnāṃ caiva bhārata
english: of Dhṛṣṭadyumna, of Bhīma, or of Śatānīka, O lord, and of all the Pāñcālas and the Cedis as well, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: eṣa karṇo raṇe pārtha pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm śarair vidhvaṃsayati vai nalinīm iva kuñjaraḥ
english: There Karṇa in battle, O Pārtha, shatters the Pāṇḍavas' host with his arrows, as an elephant tramples a bed of lotuses.

sanskrit: ete dravanti rathinas tvadīyāḥ pāṇḍunandana paśya paśya yathā pārtha gacchanty ete mahārathāḥ
english: Your chariot-warriors are fleeing, O joy of Pāṇḍu; look, look, O Pārtha, how these great chariot-warriors give way!

sanskrit: ete bhārata mātaṅgāḥ karṇenābhihatā raṇe ārtanādān vikurvāṇā vidravanti diśo daśa
english: These elephants, O Bhārata, struck down by Karṇa in the battle, uttering cries of anguish, scatter to the ten directions.

sanskrit: rathānāṃ dravatāṃ vṛndaṃ paśya pārtha samantataḥ drāvyamāṇaṃ raṇe caiva karṇenāmitrakarśinā
english: Behold on every side, O Pārtha, the host of chariots in flight, driven before him in the battle by Karṇa, that grinder of foes.

sanskrit: hastikakṣyāṃ raṇe paśya carantīṃ tatra tatra ha rathasthaṃ sūtaputrasya ketuṃ ketumatāṃ vara
english: Behold in the battle the elephant-girth pennon ranging here and there, the banner of the Sūta's son who stands upon his car, O best of those who bear banners.

sanskrit: asau dhāvati rādheyo bhīmasenarathaṃ prati kirañ śaraśatānīva vinighnaṃs tava vāhinīm
english: Yonder Rādheya rushes toward Bhīmasena's chariot, scattering as it were hundreds of arrows and smiting your host.

sanskrit: etān paśya ca pāñcālān drāvyamāṇān mahātmanā śakreṇeva yathā daityān hanyamānān mahāhave
english: Behold these Pāñcālas, driven and slain by that great-souled one in the mighty fray, as the Daityas were by Śakra.

sanskrit: eṣa karṇo raṇe jitvā pāñcālān pāṇḍusṛñjayān diśo viprekṣate sarvās tvadartham iti me matiḥ
english: Having vanquished in battle the Pāñcālas, the Pāṇḍavas, and the Sṛñjayas, Karṇa looks in every direction—seeking you, I think.

sanskrit: paśya pārtha dhanuḥ śreṣṭhaṃ vikarṣan sādhu śobhate śatrūñ jitvā yathā śakro devasaṃghaiḥ samāvṛtaḥ
english: Behold, O Pārtha, how fair he shines as he draws his peerless bow, like Śakra, having conquered his foes, surrounded by the throngs of gods.

sanskrit: ete nadanti kauravyā dṛṣṭvā karṇasya vikramam trāsayanto raṇe pārthān sṛñjayāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ
english: These Kauravas shout aloud, beholding Karṇa's prowess, terrifying in the battle the Pārthas and the Sṛñjayas by the thousands.

sanskrit: eṣa sarvātmanā pāṇḍūṃs trāsayitvā mahāraṇe abhibhāṣati rādheyaḥ sarvasainyāni mānadaḥ
english: Having with all his might struck terror into the Pāṇḍavas in the great battle, Rādheya, the honored one, addresses all the troops:

sanskrit: abhidravata gacchadhvaṃ drutaṃ dravata kauravāḥ yathā jīvan na vaḥ kaś cin mucyate yudhi sṛñjayaḥ
english: "Charge, advance, run swiftly, O Kauravas, so that no Sṛñjaya may escape from you alive in the fight!"

sanskrit: tathā kuruta saṃyattā vayaṃ yāsyāma pṛṣṭhataḥ evam uktvā yayāv eṣa pṛṣṭhato vikirañ śaraiḥ
english: "Do this, girt for the work; we shall follow at your back." Having spoken thus, he advanced behind them, scattering arrows.

sanskrit: paśya karṇaṃ raṇe pārtha śvetacchavivirājitam udayaṃ parvataṃ yadvac chobhayan vai divākaraḥ
english: Behold Karṇa in the battle, O Pārtha, radiant with his white complexion, like the day-maker sun lighting up the mountain of dawn.

sanskrit: pūrṇacandranikāśena mūrdhni chatreṇa bhārata dhriyamāṇena samare tathā śataśalākinā
english: and with the parasol borne above his head in the battle, O Bhārata, white as the full moon and ribbed with a hundred staves.

sanskrit: eṣa tvāṃ prekṣate karṇaḥ sakaṭākṣo viśāṃ pate uttamaṃ yatnam āsthāya dhruvam eṣyati saṃyuge
english: Karṇa watches for you with sidelong glance, O lord of peoples; summoning his utmost effort, he will surely come against you in the encounter.

sanskrit: paśya hy enaṃ mahābāho vidhunvānaṃ mahad dhanuḥ śarāṃś cāśīviṣākārān visṛjantaṃ mahābalam
english: Behold him, O mighty-armed one, brandishing his great bow and loosing arrows like venomous serpents, that man of vast strength.

sanskrit: asau nivṛtto rādheyo dṛśyate vānaradhvaja vadhāya cātmano 'bhyeti dīpasya śalabho yathā
english: Yonder Rādheya is seen returning, O you of the monkey banner, and he comes on to his own destruction, like a moth toward a flame.

sanskrit: karṇam ekākinaṃ dṛṣṭvā rathānīkena bhārata rirakṣiṣuḥ susaṃyatto dhārtarāṣṭro 'bhivartate
english: Seeing Karṇa alone, O Bhārata, the son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, well girt and seeking to protect him, advances with his array of chariots.

sanskrit: sārvaiḥ sahaibhir duṣṭātmā vadhya eṣa prayatnataḥ tvayā yaśaś ca rājyaṃ ca sukhaṃ cottamam icchatā
english: That evil-souled one, together with all these, must be slain with effort by you who desire glory and kingdom and the highest happiness.

sanskrit: ātmānaṃ ca kṛtātmānaṃ samīkṣya bharatarṣabha kṛtāgasaṃ ca rādheyaṃ dharmātmani yudhiṣṭhire
english: Considering yourself, your soul made perfect, O bull of the Bharatas, and Rādheya, who has done wrong against the righteous Yudhiṣṭhira—

sanskrit: pratipadyasva rādheyaṃ prāptakālam anantaram āryāṃ yuddhe matiṃ kṛtvā pratyehi rathayūthapam
english: set yourself against Rādheya, for the time has come at once; fixing your mind on the noble resolve in war, advance against that leader of chariot-bands.

sanskrit: pañca hy etāni mukhyānāṃ rathānāṃ rathasattama śatāny āyānti vegena balināṃ bhīmatejasām
english: For five hundred of these chief chariots, O best of charioteers, come on with speed, manned by the strong and dreadful in splendor.

sanskrit: pañca nāgasahasrāṇi dviguṇā vājinas tathā abhisaṃhatya kaunteya padātiprayutāni ca anyonyarakṣitaṃ vīra balaṃ tvām abhivartate
english: Five thousand elephants, twice as many horses, O son of Kuntī, and footmen by the myriad, all banded together—that host, each guarding the other, O hero, moves against you.

sanskrit: sūtaputre maheṣvāse darśayātmānam ātmanā uttamaṃ yatnam āsthāya pratyehi bharatarṣabha
english: Against the Sūta's son, that great archer, show yourself by your own might; summoning your utmost effort, O bull of the Bharatas, go forth to meet him.

sanskrit: asau karṇaḥ susaṃrabdhaḥ pāñcālān abhidhāvati ketum asya hi paśyāmi dhṛṣṭadyumnarathaṃ prati samucchetsyati pāñcālān iti manye paraṃtapa
english: Yonder Karṇa, in fury, rushes upon the Pāñcālas; for I see his banner moving toward Dhṛṣṭadyumna's chariot. He will utterly destroy the Pāñcālas, I think, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: ācakṣe te priyaṃ pārtha tad evaṃ bharatarṣabha rājā jīvati kauravyo dharmaputro yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: I tell you glad tidings, O Pārtha, and thus it is, O bull of the Bharatas: the king lives, the Kaurava Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Dharma!

sanskrit: asau bhimo mahābāhuḥ saṃnivṛttaś camūmukhe vṛtaḥ sṛñjayasainyena sātyakena ca bhārata
english: Yonder the mighty-armed Bhīma has turned back at the head of the host, surrounded by the Sṛñjaya troops and by Sātyaki, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vadhyanta ete samare kauravā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ bhīmasenena kaunteya pāñcālaiś ca mahātmabhiḥ
english: These Kauravas are being slain in the battle by sharp arrows, O son of Kuntī, by Bhīmasena and by the high-souled Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: senā hi dhārtarāṣṭrasya vimukhā cābhavad raṇāt vipradhāvati vegena bhīmasya nihatā śaraiḥ
english: For the army of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son has turned its face from the battle and flees in haste, smitten by Bhīma's arrows.

sanskrit: vipannasasyeva mahī rudhireṇa samukṣitā bhāratī bharataśreṣṭha senā kṛpaṇadarśanā
english: Like a field whose crop has failed, drenched with blood, the Bhārata army, O best of the Bharatas, is a piteous sight to behold.

sanskrit: nivṛttaṃ paśya kaunteya bhīmasenaṃ yudhāṃ patim āśīviṣam iva kruddhaṃ tasmād dravati vāhinī
english: Behold, O son of Kuntī, Bhīmasena, that lord of warriors, returned like a furious venomous serpent; before him the host takes flight.

sanskrit: pītaraktāsitasitās tārācandrārkamaṇḍitāḥ patākā viprakīryante chatrāṇy etāni cārjuna
english: Banners yellow, red, black, and white, adorned with stars, moon, and sun, are scattered abroad, and these parasols too, O Arjuna.

sanskrit: sauvarṇā rājatāś caiva taijasāś ca pṛthagvidhāḥ ketavo vinipātyante hastyaśvaṃ viprakīryate
english: Standards of gold and silver and of bright metal, of many kinds, are cast down, and the elephants and horses are scattered.

sanskrit: rathebhyaḥ prapatanty ete rathino vigatāsavaḥ nānāvarṇair hatā bāṇaiḥ pāñcālair apalāyibhiḥ
english: These chariot-warriors fall from their cars, their lives fled, slain by the many-colored arrows of the unyielding Pāñcālas.

sanskrit: nirmanuṣyān gajān aśvān rathāṃś caiva dhanaṃjaya samādravanti pāñcālā dhārtarāṣṭrāṃs tarasvinaḥ
english: The swift Pāñcālas charge upon the masterless elephants, horses, and chariots, and upon the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O Dhanaṃjaya.

sanskrit: mṛdnanti ca naravyāghrā bhīmasenavyapāśrayāt balaṃ pareṣāṃ durdharṣaṃ tyaktvā prāṇān ariṃdama
english: And those tigers among men, relying on Bhīmasena, crush the unassailable strength of the foe, recking nothing of their lives, O subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: ete nadanti pāñcālā dhamanty api ca vārijān abhidravanti ca raṇe nighnantaḥ sāyakaiḥ parān
english: These Pāñcālas roar and blow their conches, and they charge in battle, smiting their foes with arrows.

sanskrit: paśya svargasya māhātmyaṃ pāñcālā hi paraṃtapa dhārtarāṣṭrān vinighnanti kruddhāḥ siṃhā iva dvipān
english: Behold the glory of heaven, O scorcher of foes: the Pāñcālas, enraged, smite down the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra as lions slay elephants.

sanskrit: sarvataś cābhipannaiṣā dhārtarāṣṭrī mahācamūḥ pāñcālair mānasād etya haṃsair gaṅgeva vegitaiḥ
english: On every side this great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son is overwhelmed by the Pāñcālas, as the Gaṅgā is by swift swans coming from Lake Mānasa.

sanskrit: subhṛśaṃ ca parākrāntāḥ pāñcālānāṃ nivāraṇe kṛpakarṇādayo vīrā ṛṣabhāṇām ivarṣabhāḥ
english: Mightily do the heroes Kṛpa, Karṇa, and the rest exert themselves to check the Pāñcālas, like bulls among bulls.

sanskrit: sunimagnāṃś ca bhīmāstrair dhārtarāṣṭrān mahārathān dhṛṣṭadyumnamukhā vīrā ghnanti śatrūn sahasraśaḥ viṣaṇṇabhūyiṣṭharathā dhārtarāṣṭrī mahācamūḥ
english: The heroes led by Dhṛṣṭadyumna slay by the thousand those great chariot-warriors of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, deeply sunk under Bhīma's weapons; and the great host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son has its chariots for the most part downcast.

sanskrit: paśya bhīmena nārācaiś chinnā nāgāḥ patanty amī vajrivajrāhatānīva śikharāṇi mahībhṛtām
english: Behold these elephants, cleft by Bhīma's iron shafts, falling like the peaks of mountains struck by the thunderbolt of the wielder of the bolt.

sanskrit: bhīmasenasya nirviddhā bāṇaiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ svāny anīkāni mṛdnanto dravanty ete mahāgajāḥ
english: Pierced by the well-jointed arrows of Bhīmasena, these great elephants flee, trampling their own ranks.

sanskrit: nābhijānāsi bhīmasya siṃhanādaṃ durutsaham nadato 'rjuna saṃgrāme vīrasya jitakāśinaḥ
english: Do you not recognize, O Arjuna, the unbearable lion-roar of Bhīma, the hero flushed with conquest, as he shouts in the battle?

sanskrit: eṣa naiṣādir abhyeti dvipamukhyena pāṇḍavam jighāṃsus tomaraiḥ kruddho daṇḍapāṇir ivāntakaḥ
english: There the Niṣāda's son comes upon the Pāṇḍava with his lordly elephant, raging to slay him with lances, like Death with rod in hand.

sanskrit: satomarāv asya bhujau chinnau bhīmena garjataḥ tīkṣṇair agniśikhāprakhyair nārācair daśabhir hataḥ
english: His two arms, lances and all, were severed by the roaring Bhīma, and he was struck down by ten keen iron shafts bright as tongues of fire.

sanskrit: hatvainaṃ punar āyāti nāgān anyān prahāriṇaḥ paśya nīlāmbudanibhān mahāmātrair adhiṣṭhitān śaktitomarasaṃkāśair vinighnantaṃ vṛkodaram
english: Having slain him, he comes on again; behold Vṛkodara smiting other striking elephants, dark as rain-clouds and mounted by their drivers, with bolts like spears and lances.

sanskrit: sapta sapta ca nāgāṃs tān vaijayantīś ca sadhvajāḥ nihatya niśitair bāṇaiś chinnāḥ pārthāgrajena te daśabhir daśabhiś caiko nārācair nihato gajaḥ
english: Slaying seven and seven of those elephants together with their pennons and banners with sharp arrows, the elder of the Pārtha cut them down—each single elephant slain by ten iron shafts.

sanskrit: na cāsau dhārtarāṣṭrāṇāṃ śrūyate ninadas tathā puraṃdarasame kruddhe nivṛtte bharatarṣabhe
english: Nor is that clamor of the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra now heard, since that bull of the Bharatas, equal to Puraṃdara in his wrath, has returned to the fray.

sanskrit: akṣauhiṇyas tathā tisro dhārtarāṣṭrasya saṃhatāḥ kruddhena narasiṃhena bhīmasenena vāritāḥ
english: Three full divisions of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son, banded together, were thus checked by the wrathful lion among men, Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca bhīmasenena tat karma kṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā suduṣkaram arjuno vyadhamac chiṣṭān ahitān niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing that most difficult feat accomplished by Bhīmasena, Arjuna scattered the remaining foes with his keen arrows.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare saṃśaptakagaṇāḥ prabho śakrasyātithitāṃ gatvā viśokā hy abhavan mudā
english: Those bands of the saṃśaptakas, being slain in the battle, O lord, attained the guesthood of Śakra and became free of sorrow, filled with joy.

sanskrit: pārthaś ca puruṣavyāghraḥ śaraiḥ saṃnataparvabhiḥ jaghāna dhārtarāṣṭrasya caturvidhabalāṃ camūm
english: And Pārtha, that tiger among men, with his well-jointed arrows smote the fourfold host of Dhṛtarāṣṭra's son.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca nivṛtte bhīmasene ca pāṇḍave ca yudhiṣṭhire vadhyamāne bale cāpi māmake pāṇḍusṛñjayaiḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: When Bhīmasena had turned back, and the Pāṇḍava Yudhiṣṭhira too, and when my host was being slain by the Pāṇḍavas and Sṛñjayas—

sanskrit: dravamāṇe balaughe ca nirākrande muhur muhuḥ kim akurvanta kuravas tan mamācakṣva saṃjaya
english: and when the flood of my army was streaming away with cries again and again of despair—what then did the Kurus do? Tell me that, Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca dṛṣṭvā bhīmaṃ mahābāhuṃ sūtaputraḥ pratāpavān krodharaktekṣaṇo rājan bhīmasenam upādravat
english: Saṃjaya said: Beholding the mighty-armed Bhīma, the glorious son of the Sūta, his eyes red with wrath, O king, rushed upon Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: tāvakaṃ ca balaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhīmasenāt parāṅmukham yatnena mahatā rājan paryavasthāpayad balī
english: And seeing your army turning its face away from Bhīmasena, the strong one, O king, with great effort steadied it again.

sanskrit: vyavasthāpya mahābāhus tava putrasya vāhinīm pratyudyayau tadā karṇaḥ pāṇḍavān yuddhadurmadān
english: Having rallied your son's host, the mighty-armed Karṇa then went forth to meet the Pāṇḍavas, maddened with battle.

sanskrit: pratyudyayus tu rādheyaṃ pāṇḍavānāṃ mahārathāḥ dhunvānāḥ kārmukāṇy ājau vikṣipantaś ca sāyakān
english: And the great chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍavas went forth to meet Rādheya, shaking their bows in the fray and loosing their arrows.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaḥ śiner naptā śikhaṇḍī janamejayaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnaś ca balavān sarve cāpi prabhadrakāḥ
english: Bhīmasena, the grandson of Śini, Śikhaṇḍin, Janamejaya, and the strong Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and all the Prabhadrakas as well—

sanskrit: pāñcālāś ca naravyāghrāḥ samantāt tava vāhinīm abhyadravanta saṃkruddhāḥ samare jitakāśinaḥ
english: and the Pāñcālas, those tigers among men, enraged and flushed with the look of conquest in battle, charged your host on every side.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakā rājan pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm abhyadravanta tvaritā jighāṃsanto mahārathāḥ
english: And likewise your great chariot-warriors, O king, charged in haste upon the Pāṇḍavas' host, eager to slay.

sanskrit: rathanāgāśvakalilaṃ pattidhvajasamākulam babhūva puruṣavyāghra sainyam adbhutadarśanam
english: Dense with chariots, elephants, and horses, thronged with footmen and banners, the army became, O tiger among men, a wondrous sight to behold.

sanskrit: śikhaṇḍī ca yayau karṇaṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnaḥ sutaṃ tava duḥśāsanaṃ mahārāja mahatyā senayā vṛtam
english: And Śikhaṇḍin went against Karṇa, and Dhṛṣṭadyumna against your son Duḥśāsana, O great king, who was girt with a mighty host.

sanskrit: nakulo vṛṣasenaṃ ca citrasenaṃ yudhiṣṭhiraḥ ulūkaṃ samare rājan sahadevaḥ samabhyayāt
english: Nakula went against Vṛṣasena, and Yudhiṣṭhira against Citrasena, and Sahadeva, O king, advanced upon Ulūka in the battle.

sanskrit: sātyakiḥ śakuniṃ cāpi bhīmasenaś ca kauravān arjunaṃ ca raṇe yattaṃ droṇaputro mahārathaḥ
english: Sātyaki went against Śakuni, and Bhīmasena against the Kauravas, while the great chariot-warrior, the son of Droṇa, set himself against the watchful Arjuna in the battle.

sanskrit: yudhāmanyuṃ maheṣvāsaṃ gautamo 'bhyapatad raṇe kṛtavarmā ca balavān uttamaujasam ādravat
english: Gautama fell upon the great archer Yudhāmanyu in the battle, and the strong Kṛtavarman charged against Uttamaujas.
